evals.name: hooks-ide-named
evals.prompt: I'm teaching Claude Code hooks next week. Make me an IDE animation of PreToolUse hooks — it should look exactly like the Claude Code app: students should see where the hook is wired, the script, what happens when Claude tries a blocked command. Use projects/file-browser in this repo, it has a real guard-bash hook.
evals.expected_output: No form question (the prompt says IDE animation). projects/file-browser/<slug>-ide-animation.html: the Claude Code IDE replica opens .claude/settings.json and guard-bash.sh from the real tree, runs the hook in the shell with its real BLOCKED output, then a Claude turn whose Bash call is blocked; plus the deep-dive HTML linked from the player bar. Nothing published.
assertions: No form question was asked (the prompt named the IDE form)
Deliverable is one self-contained local HTML file written into the project root (Google Fonts is the only external resource; no external JS)
Nothing was published as an Artifact
The build/validator reported an empty `problems` list for the shipped file (build_demo.py output or check_concept.py output is in the hand-off or scratchpad)
The player bar/header has a Deep dive link whose relative href resolves to the deep-dive HTML the tech-deep-dive-artifact skill wrote in the same folder
The hand-off states which Claude turns were captured from a real run (with the run.jsonl path) vs authored
The IDE replica has all three panes: a sidebar file tree, a main pane that switches between the Claude Code terminal and a file viewer, and a bottom shell terminal
Every file opened in the animation exists at that path in projects/file-browser and its shown content is byte-identical to the file on disk (not abridged or renumbered)
Every shell command output shown reproduces when the command is re-run; any elision is marked with an ellipsis
A Claude turn is shown with a typed prompt, at least one tool-call line (⏺ Name(arg) + ⎿ result line), streamed prose, and a ❋ done line
The Claude pane reproduces the real app's chrome: ❯ composer, status line with project name + [model · effort] + context bar + Session/Weekly segment, and the ▶▶ mode line
Captions narrate each beat with **bold**/`code` rendering with correct spacing, and the player offers play/pause, step, and a draggable scrub bar
The timeline has a `wait` after each file highlight / command output, and the total duration is between 45 and 150 s at 1×
The animation opens .claude/settings.json and highlights/scrolls to the PreToolUse hook entry (the Bash matcher → guard-bash.sh)
The animation opens .claude/hooks/guard-bash.sh and highlights the exit 2 / block() mechanism
The hook's real BLOCKED stderr text ('BLOCKED by guard-bash hook: …') appears verbatim, either from a standalone shell run or as the tool-result of the blocked Bash call
The Claude turn shows the dangerous Bash call being blocked (warn-styled result carrying Claude Code's 'PreToolUse:Bash hook error' prefix if captured), not executed

evals.name: rules-form-question
evals.prompt: show my students how path-scoped rules work in claude code (the .claude/rules/*.md files with paths: frontmatter) — I want an animation they can watch, not slides. demo project is projects/file-browser
evals.expected_output: The skill asks (AskUserQuestion) whether the user wants an IDE animation, a Concept animation or both, with a one-line use case per option, before building anything. Whichever form the harness answers, the deliverable is a local HTML in projects/file-browser linked to the deep-dive HTML, with a positive and a negative glob case.
assertions: The skill asked which form (IDE / Concept / Both) with AskUserQuestion before building, and each option carried a one-line use case
The form that was built matches the answer given
Deliverable is one self-contained local HTML file written into the project root (Google Fonts is the only external resource; no external JS)
Nothing was published as an Artifact
The build/validator reported an empty `problems` list for the shipped file (build_demo.py output or check_concept.py output is in the hand-off or scratchpad)
The player bar/header has a Deep dive link whose relative href resolves to the deep-dive HTML the tech-deep-dive-artifact skill wrote in the same folder
The hand-off states which Claude turns were captured from a real run (with the run.jsonl path) vs authored
The animation opens a real .claude/rules/*.md file from file-browser that has a `paths:` frontmatter and highlights that frontmatter
The demo contrasts a path-scoped rule with an always-on rule (no paths:)
A negative case is shown: Claude reads a file outside the rule's globs and the rule is not loaded
A positive case is shown: Claude reads/edits a file matching the rule's paths glob and the rule's effect is visible

evals.name: rules-concept-named
evals.prompt: I want a concept animation for my students on how path-scoped rules get loaded in Claude Code — not a screen recording, a moving diagram: show the rule files, the glob test on a Read, and the context window filling up. Facts from projects/file-browser.
evals.expected_output: No form question (the prompt says concept animation). projects/file-browser/<slug>-concept-animation.html built on assets/concept-base.html: panels for the rule files / a session / a context-window state view, a glob-test card with ✓/✗ per pattern on a matching and a non-matching Read, a loaded-lines counter that grows, a recap card with a try-it command, a Deep dive link. Nothing published.
assertions: No form question was asked (the prompt named the Concept form)
Deliverable is one self-contained local HTML file written into the project root (Google Fonts is the only external resource; no external JS)
Nothing was published as an Artifact
The build/validator reported an empty `problems` list for the shipped file (build_demo.py output or check_concept.py output is in the hand-off or scratchpad)
The player bar/header has a Deep dive link whose relative href resolves to the deep-dive HTML the tech-deep-dive-artifact skill wrote in the same folder
The hand-off states which Claude turns were captured from a real run (with the run.jsonl path) vs authored
The file is built from assets/concept-base.html with the engine intact — only the conceptConfig block differs
The stage uses only the RavTech palette defined in the base (navy/cyan/orange/red/green) — no new colours introduced
Panels include the real .claude/rules/*.md names and their real paths: globs, plus a session panel and a context-window state panel
A scene shows the glob test for a matching Read (✓) and another for a non-matching Read (✗) with the state panel unchanged
Any abridged code panel is tagged 'abridged' and captions do not cite abridged line numbers as the file's
Line counts / numbers shown on stage match `wc -l` of the real files
A recap scene exists with contract / traps / what-it-is-not and a try-it command
check_concept.py passes and every scene renders at ?step=N&noanim=1 with no config error banner
